facts.raw_span: A 32-year-old African American female
elevated intraocular pressure at age 13
taller stature than her relatives (180.4 cm)
long fingers
hypermobility of the shoulders, digits, and knees
Family history was negative for similar findings
Serial echocardiograms showed no abnormalities
Open iridocorneal angle in each eye
No evidence of Haab striae, buphthalmos, or high iris insertion
Subtle lens dislocation superonasally in the right eye (first observed at age 17)
Later developed lens dislocation in the left eye (at age 32)
2 heterozygous variants in the LTBP2 gene (c.709C>T p.Arg237* and c.3776-1G>C splice acceptor)

concepts.why: The patient's tall stature, long fingers, and hypermobility are consistent with Homocystinuria, and the lens dislocation is a known complication of this condition.
The patient's lens dislocation and hypermobility are consistent with Weill-Marchesani Syndrome, although the tall stature and long fingers are not typical of this condition.
The patient's hypermobility is consistent with Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, although the lens dislocation is not a typical feature of this condition.

The patient's tall stature, long fingers, and hypermobility are consistent with Marfan Syndrome, although the absence of cardiac abnormalities and the presence of lens dislocation are not typical of this condition.

The patient's elevated intraocular pressure and open iridocorneal angle are consistent with Pseudoexfoliation Syndrome, although the absence of exfoliative material on the lens is not typical of this condition.

The patient's elevated intraocular pressure and open iridocorneal angle are consistent with Primary Congenital Glaucoma, although the absence of Haab striae and buphthalmos is not typical of this condition.
The patient's lens dislocation is consistent with Ectopia Lentis, which can occur in isolation or as part of a systemic condition.
The patient's genetic testing revealed two heterozygous variants in the LTBP2 gene, which is consistent with an LTBP2-related disorder.

rationales.F02: Elevated intraocular pressure is a key feature of Primary Congenital Glaucoma and can be associated with other conditions.
rationales.F04: Long fingers are a characteristic feature of several connective tissue disorders, including Weill-Marchesani Syndrome and Marfan Syndrome.
rationales.F05: Hypermobility is a hallmark of Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome and can also be seen in other conditions.
rationales.F07: Normal echocardiograms decrease the likelihood of Marfan Syndrome, which often involves cardiac abnormalities.
rationales.F09: The absence of Haab striae, buphthalmos, or high iris insertion makes Primary Congenital Glaucoma less likely.
rationales.F10: Lens dislocation is a feature of Homocystinuria, Weill-Marchesani Syndrome, and Marfan Syndrome, among others.
rationales.F12: The presence of LTBP2 gene variants strongly suggests an LTBP2-related disorder.
